_comment: The routing contract for ci-land. `route` is the skill that must answer the prompt (`none` means no skill: the human or the repo's own review bot); `why` records the rule that decides it. Pinned by tests/test_ci_land_contract.py.

routings.why: the named job: open PR to green checks and handled threads
one PR, failing checks to fix and push

routings.prompt: deal with the bugbot comments and get this green
routings.why: review bot findings on one PR, fixed in one batch

routings.prompt: finish the review loop on my PR
routings.why: the last mile after the code is done
naming the skill reaches the skill

routings.prompt: address the CodeRabbit threads and push
routings.why: review threads on one PR, fixed and pushed to its own branch
repo-wide speed audit, not one PR
repo-wide configuration grade, not one PR
repo-wide security audit, not one PR
diagnosing one run from a pasted Actions URL
finding bugs is the review bot's job; ci-land only acts on posted findings
merging is the human's call; ci-land never merges

routings.prompt: bugbot keeps finding stuff on #58 every time i push one fix. do them all at once and get the checks passing
routings.why: repeated bot findings on one PR, wants them batched into one pass

routings.prompt: can you get this thing mergeable? the PR is open on my current branch and cubic already reviewed it
routings.why: mergeable phrasing for the current branch's PR, with a named bot reviewer

routings.prompt: babysit PR 213 until it merges and ping me if anything goes red
routings.why: watching a PR until it merges is outside ci-land's bounded budget

routings.prompt: fix what the bots got right and push once
routings.why: verified bot findings on one PR, batched into a single push

routings.prompt: finish the review loop even though this session is almost out of context
routings.why: the last mile after the code is done, handed to a background driver
